sources.quote: Lippmann was born on 16 August 1845 in Hollerich, in Hollerich, in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
Later, the entire family moved to Paris, where Gabriel received his early education.
In 1858, Lippmann followed the "Lycée Napoléon" (today known as Henri-IV).
Under the influence of Almeida, Lippmann headed the scientific section of the "École normale" (normal school), which he entered in 1868 at the age of 23.
Lippmann was then named a professor at the Sorbonne University and head of the laboratory of physics.
The inventor of color photography was a member of the French Academy of Sciences in 1886 and was elected as its president in 1912.
He was a member of the "Société francaise de photographie" (1892) and its president (1896e1899).
Lippmann was one of the founders of the "Institut d'optique théorique et appliquée" in France.
He was also known for his discovery of heliochromes, microscopic analyses, and of the Lippmann electrometer.

Jonas Ferdinand Gabriel Lippmann, a Luxembourgish-French physicist, is known for the innovation he brought to the color reproduction method in photography and for having produced the first color photographic plate.
For this work, he was the Nobel laureate in physics in 1908.
The high culture of Lippmann was further refined in the circles that he frequented after his marriage (1888) to the daughter of Victor Cherbuliez (novelist and author).
One of his more interesting collaborations was with the young Polish student Marie Skłodowska (Curie), as well as with Maurice Couette and Pierre Curie.

It must be mentioned that Herman von Helmholtz was also an academic advisor.

However, the Public Research Centree Gabriel Lippmann later merged with the Public Research Centre e Henri Tudor on 1 January 2015, and formed the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST).
